<reason>A better established why readiness checks and subsequent enforcement are complementary. B exposed genuine friction in requiring stronger plans across all three areas, but repeatedly treated imperfect verification as worthless verification. A answered with proportionate commitments using existing services and honestly accepted denial where transport remained genuinely unworkable. B’s transport answer instead assumed alternatives that A already permitted. Administrative burdens remained a live objection, but B did not establish that they outweighed preparation’s preventive value.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s closing response to the cleanup-rota argument was decisive: confirming that someone is assigned and available cannot guarantee cleanliness, but can prevent discovering that nobody was responsible only after the failure. This directly undermined B’s claim that both approaches create an identical risk window.</best_rebuttal>
